title: Google Cloud CLI configuration
whyItMatters: The gcloud folder holds OAuth tokens, cached credentials and the active account for Google Cloud. A stranger could use them to act as the account owner in the cloud.
source: Google Cloud docs, Managing gcloud CLI configurations: configurations live in %APPDATA%/gcloud on Windows - https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/configurations
notes: Covers credentials.db, access_tokens.db and the configurations folder. CLOUDSDK_CONFIG can move the folder; file contents are not read. Revoking the account access is what actually stops the tokens working.

cleanup.signOut: Remove the Google Cloud SDK from Third-party apps and services in the Google Account settings, so the tokens stored on this PC stop working.
steps: Remove access for the Google Cloud SDK in the Google Account security settings.
Close any open command prompt where gcloud was used.
Delete the folder named in the plan if it is still there.
cleanup.risk: Removes the saved Google Cloud logins and settings from this PC. Tokens that are not revoked in the Google Account keep working from anywhere.
cleanup.source: Google Cloud docs, Authenticate for the gcloud CLI: https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/authenticate
